about: Same five-step ladder as reviews.json (see its 'about'). {X} = the name he picks or types; {a}/{plural} = the kind of thing. 'against' marks the other side (the empty square on the card). · 25 Nov 2026 (the owner, after the content check): every way is a phrase the task's own model texts use (the Model and Guided/Sample steps), three alternatives per move, the moves in the models' order, so Basics teaches what the practice shows. · 'example' on a subject: the five sentences finished for its first answer (eg), each starting with its move's first way; Basics shows them on its card (25 Nov 2026, the owner: immediately likeable).
name: Email
how: An email to a friend in five sentences, as the model emails do: open warmly, your main point, the details, the other side, and a friendly ending.

nameAsk.title: Who to?
nameAsk.aim: Pick a name. You’ll write to this friend.

notebook: Write your email to {X} in five sentences, one per slot. Then check:
ticks: I greeted my friend by name.
I answered every question in their email.
I signed off like a friend.

subjects.label: Giving advice
example: Hi Sam, thanks for your email — I'm so glad you asked me for advice.
I'm writing because I had the same problem last year.
Here's what I'm thinking: talk to your teacher after class tomorrow.
On the other hand, you might want to ask your parents first.
Let me know what suits you best.

subjects.label: An invitation
subjects.ask: when? where? what will you do?
example: Hi Alex, thanks for your email — I'm so glad you're coming to Funchal!
I'm writing because I'd love you to come to my birthday party on Saturday.
Here's what I'm thinking: we could go to the beach in the afternoon.
On the other hand, you might want to rest after your trip.
Let me know what suits you best.

subjects.label: Your news
example: Hi Maria, thanks for your email — I'm so glad you passed your exams!
I'm writing because I've got some big news too.
Here's what I'm thinking: we should celebrate together next weekend.
On the other hand, you might want to stay at home with your family.
Let me know what suits you best.

subjects.label: Saying thank you
subjects.ask: for what? why was it great?
example: Hi Tom, thanks for your email — I'm so glad you enjoyed your visit.
I'm writing because I wanted to say thank you for the lovely present.
Here's what I'm thinking: you should come again in the summer.
On the other hand, you might want to visit in winter, when it's quieter.
Let me know what suits you best.
